title: Using AI in Advertising During Peak Season
summary: AI Max, Performance Max and Smart Bidding can all help during peak, but only with the right signals and guardrails. Here’s how to set them up.
body_markdown:
Peak season moves quickly. Search demand changes, competition increases, best-selling products shift, and the decisions that matter most often need to be made in days rather than weeks.


Google Ads AI can help brands respond faster, but the best results do not come from turning on every available feature. They come from giving the platform clear business signals, sensible guardrails and enough time to learn before the peak period begins.


For most ecommerce brands, there are four areas where AI can make the biggest difference.


## **1. Find demand you may not be targeting today**


During a sale period, customers often search in ways that are different from the rest of the year. They may use broader category terms, compare options, search for gifts or add urgency around delivery and availability.


[AI Max for Search](https://au.pattern.com/blog/google-ai-overviews-ads/) can help capture this changing demand. It expands beyond a fixed keyword list to identify additional relevant searches, helping brands appear when customers use terms that were not included in the original campaign build.


This is especially useful for brands with tightly managed Search campaigns. Rather than replacing the existing keyword strategy, AI Max can be tested alongside it to identify whether the additional search coverage is bringing in valuable traffic.


The important part is maintaining control. Brand exclusions, negative keywords and location settings should be reviewed before the feature is activated, and performance should be tested before rolling it out more broadly.


## **2. Help the platform understand what a valuable sale looks like**


Not every conversion has the same value during peak season.


A full-price purchase may be more profitable than a heavily discounted item. A new customer may be worth more than a returning customer. Some products may need additional investment because they have healthy stock and stronger margins, while others may need to be protected.


Google’s bidding systems can make better decisions when they are given this context.


Accurate conversion values, Customer Match lists and product information help the platform prioritise the sales that matter most to the business. This is particularly important for Performance Max, where Google is making bidding and placement decisions across multiple channels in real time.


The goal is not simply to maximise revenue. It is to guide investment towards the customers and products that create the best commercial outcome.


## **3. Scale with more control**


Peak season often creates a difficult trade-off. Brands want to capture more demand, but do not want to sacrifice profitability just to increase spend.


Smart Bidding helps manage this balance by adjusting bids in real time based on the likelihood that a user will convert. For established campaigns, Smart Bidding Exploration can also help the platform test new search opportunities while maintaining a clear efficiency target.


This is more useful than making large, blanket changes to campaign targets. A sudden reduction in Target ROAS can open the account up too broadly. Controlled exploration gives the platform room to find new demand without changing the entire approach.


The best time to test this is before the sales period begins. Peak season should be the time to scale what is working, not the first time a new strategy is introduced.


## **4. Use reporting to keep AI accountable**


AI should not mean less visibility.


Google Ads now provides more ways to understand how Performance Max is delivering results, including channel performance, search-term insights and campaign diagnostics. These reports help identify whether a campaign is finding value in Search, Shopping, YouTube or other Google channels, and where performance may be limited by budget, feed issues or campaign settings.


During peak season, the focus should be on a small number of commercial signals:


- Is the campaign limited by budget while meeting its efficiency target?


- Are the right products in stock and available to serve?


- Is conversion value growing alongside spend?


- Are new search terms relevant to the brand?


- Are new customers being acquired at an acceptable cost?


This keeps decision-making focused on business outcomes rather than reacting to every daily movement in the account.


## **Preparing for peak season**


The best preparation starts early.


In the weeks before peak, brands should confirm that conversion tracking, product feeds and customer data are accurate. This is also the right time to test AI Max, review Performance Max settings and forecast likely budget requirements.


[Get your complimentary product feed audit here.](https://go.pattern.com/2026-01PatternFeedOptimisationTool_RegistrationPage.html)


In the middle of peak, changes should be measured and deliberate. Avoid launching entirely new campaigns or changing budgets, targets and targeting settings all at once. It becomes difficult to know what is driving the result.


For short promotional periods, such as a flash sale, seasonality adjustments can help Smart Bidding account for an expected short-term change in conversion rate. For longer periods, it is usually better to let the system respond to normal seasonal demand while the team monitors performance closely.


## **The takeaway**


AI is most valuable during peak season when it helps brands make faster, better-informed decisions.


AI Max can uncover demand that a standard keyword strategy may miss. Performance Max can prioritise the customers and products that matter most. Smart Bidding can respond to changing auction conditions in real time.


The brands that perform best will be the ones that prepare early, give the platform clear commercial signals and keep the right controls in place as demand increases.
